lead: A foreign king in Genesis listens to God in a dream, while Abraham, the friend of God, tells a half-truth out of fear. The Epistle (Romans 2:12–16) then speaks of Gentiles who show that “what the law requires is written on their hearts”. In Luke, Jesus calls for open witness and promises that the Holy Spirit will teach us what to say. The readings ask whether we will speak truthfully when we are afraid, and they assure us that God is not limited to the people we expect him to work through.

set: Abraham moves south to the Negeb, and lives as an alien at Gerar. This is the second of three stories in Genesis in which a patriarch passes off his wife as his sister (12:10–20; 26:6–11). Many scholars think they are forms of an old tradition retold in different settings. As they stand, they show that faith does not remove fear overnight.

The timing makes the danger greater. Abraham has just been promised that Sarah will bear a son (18:10). If she is lost now, so is the promise. God himself steps in to protect what Abraham has put at risk.
str: vv. 1–2: Abraham's half-truth; Sarah is taken.
v. 3: God comes to Abimelech in a dream.
vv. 6–7: God answers: he knows, he has restrained him, and Abraham must pray.
kw: Wholeness, with nothing divided. A foreign king is the one who uses this phrase here, and God accepts it.
This is the first time the word appears in the Bible, and it is used of Abraham. Here the mark of a prophet is not foretelling, but that he “will pray for you”.
vv: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night,
God speaks to a king outside the covenant. He is not bound to the boundaries that we draw.
Lord, will you destroy an innocent people?
In Hebrew the word for “innocent” is the same as Abraham's word for “righteous” in 18:23. The foreign king now asks God Abraham's own question.
furthermore it was I who kept you from sinning against me.
A striking insight: God's care lies behind even the sins we have not committed. The king's innocence is in part God's gift.
for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you shall live.
God gives Abraham, who has just failed, the task of interceding for the man he wronged. His weakness has not cancelled his calling.
ch: The Second Vatican Council teaches that deep within the conscience a person discovers a law he has not laid on himself, which he must obey, and that conscience is man's most secret core and sanctuary, where he is alone with God (Gaudium et Spes 16; CCC 1776). The Church also teaches that those who, through no fault of their own, do not know the Gospel, but seek God with a sincere heart and try to do his will, can attain salvation (Lumen Gentium 16). Abimelech is an early picture of this.

r.h: The Spirit will teach you what to say
set: Jesus is on his way to Jerusalem, and thousands are gathering (12:1). He warns the disciples against hypocrisy and against fear of those who can kill only the body (12:1–7). These verses continue: the one who fears God can speak openly before others. The “synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities” in verse 11 cover every sort of court, Jewish and Gentile alike, that the first disciples came to know.
str: v. 10: the word against the Son of Man and the blasphemy against the Spirit.
vv. 11–12: do not worry; the Spirit will teach.
kw: To say the same thing, to confess publicly. It is the word for what the Church does in her creed.
To speak against, to slander. See the question below about the sin against the Holy Spirit.
The courtroom word, from which “apologetics” comes. The disciple does not have to prepare this alone.
vv: everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God;
A word said on earth has an echo in heaven. Jesus describes himself as a witness who speaks for those who spoke for him.
whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
A word against the Son of Man can be forgiven, and Peter, who denied him and was prayed for, is the proof (Luke 22:32). This is something else: see the question below.
for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.
Spoken to frightened people, not to clever ones. Many martyrs' accounts show simple believers answering judges with surprising clarity.
ch: The Catechism teaches that the disciple of Christ must not only keep the faith and live on it, but also profess it, confidently bear witness to it, and spread it, and it quotes the parallel saying from Matthew 10:32–33 (CCC 1816). Those who belong to Christ through faith and Baptism must confess their baptismal faith before others (CCC 14).

qa: What is the sin against the Holy Spirit? Have I committed it?

The Catechism explains it this way: there are no limits to the mercy of God, but anyone who deliberately refuses to accept his mercy by repenting rejects the forgiveness of his sins and the salvation offered by the Holy Spirit (CCC 1864). So it is not a particular word said in anger, or a terrible thought that comes to a troubled mind. It is a closed door kept shut from the inside. Anyone who fears having committed it, and is sorry, is showing that the door is not shut.
study: When has fear led me to say something less than the truth? What did it put at risk?
Who has shown me integrity of heart from outside my own community? What can I learn from it?
